# .github/workflows

What GitHub runs for the repository: its Actions. (`.github/` itself has no README: GitHub would show it as the repository's front page instead of the root's.) Cloudflare Pages builds the site itself, from the two stage branches only, which `ci.yml` moves.

- `ci.yml` (workflow "CI"): every push to `main` renders the voice sprites, checks types and duplicates, runs the unit tests and the site's build on x64 Linux, and the unit tests again on ARM Linux and on macOS (the job `platforms`: the shared world and the bits the tests pin must come out alike on every processor and system, see `src/detmath.ts`); only a commit that passes them all goes on to `stage_test` and, while `PROMOTE_PROD` is on (no players yet), `stage_prod`. Its sprites go up to the release `voice-sprites` under their inputs' key with a pointer per commit (the newest 30 kept), which names the SHA-256 of each file as stored, a render of the same key kept before included, and Cloudflare's build takes them from there (`tools/voice/prebuilt.ts`). The check and platforms jobs, which run our code and its packages, may only read; the publish job, which runs nothing but the shell, jq, git and gh, writes the release and the two branches. A newer push cancels an older run.

- `voice.yml` (workflow "Voice"): clones the lines of Nicole and the campaign's people (Rask, Pim, Hedda, the Saw Brothers) into German, Spanish and French whenever the lines, their translations or the clone tools change on `main`, or by hand (Actions → Voice → Run workflow), and keeps them as assets of the release `voice-nicole`. The clone jobs, which run Chatterbox, Whisper and their packages, may only read; a separate upload job, which runs no code of others, checks each store they hand on and writes the release. See `tools/voice/README.md`.
- `relays.yml` (workflow "Relays"): every Monday, and by hand, checks the public Nostr relays of the online tournament (`npm run relays`) and commits `src/net/relays.json` to `main` when the healthy relays changed. Two jobs: the check, which runs Trystero's code and reads the relays' answers, may only read and hands the list on as its output; the commit, in a fresh checkout, runs nothing but the shell, jq, git and gh, holds the `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: write` and `actions: write`, and starts the workflow CI for the new commit (a push with that token starts none by itself). It installs without install scripts and holds no other secret. See `tools/relays/README.md`.
- `cla.yml`: checks every pull request for the signed Contributor License Agreement (`contributors/<login>.txt`, see `CONTRIBUTING.md`), labels it `cla: missing` or `cla: signed` and comments when that changes. It never runs code from the pull request.

The actions they use are pinned to their commits, and each job gets only the permissions it needs.
